A1.justification: Both are readable 12-page versions of the same TDFusion paper, supporting comparison of the text, equations, figures and tables. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement; separately cited supplementary material is outside the supplied evidence.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-fusion, semantic-segmentation and object-detection experiments, including quantitative comparisons, qualitative examples and ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–5.

M1.justification: The learnable intensity weights, gradient loss, alternating meta-learning updates, network architectures and training procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 receives wording and punctuation corrections without changing its steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate fusion on MSRS, FMB, M3FD and LLVIP, segmentation on MSRS/FMB, and detection on M3FD/LLVIP. The FMB/LLVIP-to-MSRS task-preference analysis is also retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain TarDAL, SegMIF, MURF, EMMA, DCINN, MRFS and TIMFusion. Table 2 also retains the infrared-only and visible-only comparisons. Added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, subsampling, evaluation metrics and model settings are unchanged. Both report 50 training epochs, 200 loss-generation-module iterations, and 300-epoch downstream-network retraining.

E4.justification: Sections 4.4–4.5 retain the same task-preference analysis and five FMB ablations, with unchanged Figure 5 and Table 3 evidence. V2 adds a pointer to supplementary visualizations and analysis, but supplies no additional analysis within these PDFs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The uncertainty-reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All 308 result values in Tables 1–3 match. For example, Table 2 retains TDFusion's FMB mIoU of 60.50 and M3FD mAP50 of 86.27. The qualitative examples, rankings and reported findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11) and the Section 3.7 derivation are retained. V2 explicitly connects the explanatory prose to the existing (a)/(b) labels, without changing mathematical definitions, assumptions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about task-guided learnable fusion loss, architectural flexibility, task-specific information preferences and performance across four datasets. Wording edits do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Both versions give the same interpretations of detail preservation, downstream performance and task-dependent weighting, including segmentation boundaries and detection contrast in Section 4.4. No substantive limitation, applicability boundary or mechanism explanation is added.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from promising a future code release to stating that code is available and providing a TDFusion GitHub address. Implementation settings, hardware descriptions and dataset-split information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 73 to 89 entries, mainly through additions to existing citation clusters. Section 2.2 adds a brief explanation of the already-cited ReFusion's reconstruction-guided learnable loss and removes the U2Fusion/meta-learning analogy. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract, introduction and several later passages, corrects small wording errors, expands the Section 2.1 heading, and adds an acknowledgement and another corresponding-author marker. The section sequence and main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The five figures and three tables are retained. Algorithm 1 moves from page 6 to page 5, Table 3 shifts within page 8, table highlighting becomes stronger, the QAB/F notation is standardized, and Figure 5's caption is revised.

improvement.justification: V2 provides a repository address instead of a release promise, explains the relationship to ReFusion more clearly, and improves wording and table legibility. These are useful, limited gains in documentation and presentation; the method, theory and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
